text:
jonah: heads-up: saw a weird production-like repro in samples where multiple concurrent Retrofit calls on emulator hang behind the dispatcher and eventually fail with timeout. physical device not affected.

maya: hmm. what's the symptom? are requests queued or getting 503s?

jonah: queued. root cause appears to be default OkHttp Dispatcher limits (64/5) combined with an Authenticator that does a blocking refresh using the same client. On emulator the network is slower so refreshes pile up and exhaust dispatcher threads.

sanjay: oh yeah, if the Authenticator uses the same client's dispatcher it competes for the same connection threads. Any snippet?

jonah: simplified pattern: Interceptor notices 401 -> calls blocking refresh using `client.newCall(refreshReq).execute()` on the same client. Meanwhile many other calls wait for dispatcher threads -> starvation -> timeouts.

maya: quick fixes: 1) use a dedicated OkHttpClient for token refresh with its own Dispatcher/Executor; 2) increase Dispatcher.maxRequests/ maxRequestsPerHost in samples; 3) make refresh non-blocking so it doesn't consume dispatcher threads.

jonah: example for dedicated client: ```kotlin
val authDispatcher = Dispatcher(Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor())
val authClient = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .dispatcher(authDispatcher)
  .connectionPool(ConnectionPool(0,1,TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS))
  .callTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(20))
  .build()
```

sanjay: also suggest adding a runtime assertion in SDK samples that logs when activeCalls > threshold so devs see dispatcher exhaustion early.

maya: for docs we should add a checklist: "If you hit request hang on emulator: check Dispatcher limits, avoid blocking refresh on same client, use separate auth client, or prefetch tokens." Include code samples.

jonah: opened branch maya/dispatcher-auth-sample with a small sample and CI emulator job. ciara-bot queued the run.

ciara-bot: CI started for branch maya/dispatcher-auth-sample : emulator (api29) matrix queued.

sanjay: tiny SDK idea: provide a convenience helper `AuthClients.createDefault()` that returns a safe, non-pooling client for use in Authenticators. That will reduce common footguns.

maya: agree. I'll add that helper to samples and document it in the Kotlin SDK FAQ.

jonah: thanks all. follow-up: add a unit test that simulates dispatcher exhaustion using a small thread pool so we catch regressions.
